answer: Retroactive fraud windows keep every payout locked for 30 days before it unbonds. Anyone who submits a duplication proof in that window claims half the slashed bond; the rest burns. So N fakes leave N separate 30-day balances exposed to bounty hunters paid from the attacker's own collateral, and those locks cannot be pooled into one wallet. An honest seat cashing out after pricing nectar syrup, grading ivory piano keys, or bidding walnut timber keeps the coin once the window closes.
